a framework for highly available network services can be implemented in the Linux kernel by allowing network interfaces to be backed up by other network interfaces and inter-server I/O links, and by enabling the server to take over another server's packet transmission job when the latter server's network interface has failed.
HANet allows network services to continue operating when all their public interfaces to the outside have failed.
